The test image shows: white cottony mycelium covering a stem base, with numerous small spherical yellowish/tan sclerotia embedded throughout the mycelium. This is strongly characteristic of Southern Blight (Sclerotium rolfsii).

Let me confirm with one reference image.

The reference image shows a later-stage stem canker from Southern Blight. The test image shows an earlier/different angle with the diagnostic features clearly visible:

- **Dense white cottony mycelium** radiating from the stem base (signature Southern Blight feature)
- **Numerous small spherical sclerotia** (tan/yellow, mustard-seed sized) embedded throughout the mycelium

These two features together are pathognomonic for Southern Blight (Sclerotium rolfsii). Sclerotinia Timber Rot has similar white mycelium but produces much larger, rice-grain-sized, grayish-black sclerotia — not the small tan ones visible here.
